name: Jehoram of Judah
charge: Slaying all his brethren with the sword as soon as he was strengthened; walking in the way of the house of Ahab, for he had the daughter of Ahab to wife; making high places and compelling Judah to fornication
summary: As soon as Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat had the throne he killed all his brothers; married to Ahab’s daughter, he walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, made high places and compelled Judah to fornication (2 Chronicles 21:1-11). Edom and Libnah revolted, a writing from Elijah pronounced a plague on his house and a disease of his bowels, and Philistines and Arabians carried off his goods, wives and sons (2 Chronicles 21:8-17). After two years his bowels fell out, and he died without being desired (2 Chronicles 21:18-20).
offenseFull: Jehoshaphat gave his other sons great gifts of silver, gold and fenced cities, but the kingdom to Jehoram because he was the firstborn. As soon as Jehoram had risen up and strengthened himself, he killed all his brothers with the sword, and some of the princes of Israel too (2 Chronicles 21:1-4). This is a pattern to watch: as soon as some among Israel get power, they turn and hurt everyone around them; at thirty-two, all he could think of was killing anyone he saw as a threat. He reigned eight years and walked in the way of the kings of Israel as the house of Ahab did, for he had Ahab’s daughter to wife (2 Chronicles 21:5-6). A wicked man is given a wicked woman: her mother was the one who had Naboth killed for his vineyard. Second Chronicles is the same history as 2 Kings 8, told again the way the gospels retell one story (2 Kings 8:16-18).

He made high places in the mountains of Judah, caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit fornication and compelled Judah to it (2 Chronicles 21:11). High places are places of worship that have nothing to do with the God of Israel. Dealing with other gods is spiritual fornication, but physical fornication is built into these false worships; the pagan holidays passed down to our people are built on it, and that is what draws the people. Then a writing came to him from Elijah the prophet: because he had not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat or Asa, but had led Judah into the same spiritual whoredom as the house of Ahab, and had killed his brothers who were better than himself, the Lord would strike his people, his children, his wives and all his goods with a great plague, and he would have a disease of the bowels until they fell out day by day (2 Chronicles 21:12-15). Everyone who follows an evil man shares in it when judgment comes on him, and the Lord

touches whatever sustains you. This is what it looks like to mess with the Most High: every sickness not written in the book of the law He brings on a disobedient people (Deuteronomy 28:61), and many are weak and sickly for disobedience (1 Corinthians 11:30).
judgmentFull: In his days Edom revolted from under Judah and made itself a king, and Libnah revolted at the same time, because he had forsaken the Lord God of his fathers (2 Chronicles 21:8-10). When we obey the Most High the nations are subject to us; when we come out from under the commandments they rise up. We had Esau on lockdown around Petra, and this was the word to Esau coming due, that when he had the dominion he would break Jacob’s yoke from his neck (Genesis 27:40). From that revolt Edom increased in numbers and strength and spread its colonies far and wide.

The Lord stirred up the Philistines and the Arabians near the Ethiopians, and they broke into Judah, carried away all the substance of the king’s house, his sons and his wives, and left him only Jehoahaz, the youngest (2 Chronicles 21:16-17). Ham and Ishmael raided Judah together, and the scholars note that it accords with Joel, where the children of Judah were sold to the Grecians (Joel 3:4-6); the same peoples later held our people in the trans-Saharan slave trade. Then the Lord struck him in his bowels with an incurable disease, and after two years his bowels fell out and he died of grievous diseases, the sickness working from within like the cancers of today. His people made no burning for him as for his fathers; he departed without being desired, buried in the city of David but not in the sepulchres of the kings (2 Chronicles 21:18-20). Many were glad to see him go. A good name is better than precious ointment (Ecclesiastes 7:1); a man cannot rule wickedly and shame the people and expect them to stand by him when disease comes. It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God (Hebrews 10:31).

Yet the Lord would not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant He made to give a light to him and his sons for ever (2 Chronicles 21:7). The Most High keeps His promises, to David as to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. That is why a man who wakes up to the truth must not go off: a righteous father’s walk preserves his lineage, and a wicked one can destroy a whole line.

text.text: Now Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. And Jehoram his son reigned in his stead.
And he had brethren the sons of Jehoshaphat, Azariah, and Jehiel, and Zechariah, and Azariah, and Michael, and Shephatiah: all these were the sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.
And their father gave them great gifts of silver, and of gold, and of precious things, with fenced cities in Judah: but the kingdom gave he to Jehoram; because he was the firstborn.
Now when Jehoram was risen up to the kingdom of his father, he strengthened himself, and slew all his brethren with the sword, and divers also of the princes of Israel.
Jehoram was thirty and two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, like as did the house of Ahab: for he had the daughter of Ahab to wife: and he wrought that which was evil in the eyes of the Lord.
Howbeit the Lord would not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that he had made with David, and as he promised to give a light to him and to his sons for ever.
In his days the Edomites revolted from under the dominion of Judah, and made themselves a king.
Then Jehoram went forth with his princes, and all his chariots with him: and he rose up by night, and smote the Edomites which compassed him in, and the captains of the chariots.
So the Edomites revolted from under the hand of Judah unto this day. The same time also did Libnah revolt from under his hand; because he had forsaken the Lord God of his fathers.

And thou shalt have great sickness by disease of thy bowels, until thy bowels fall out by reason of the sickness day by day.
